Visualization gallery

Source: vignettes/visualization.Rmd
visualization.Rmd

This vignette walks through every plotting function in micropubr. Each returns a ggplot2 object you can extend with +, share a common set of arguments (group.by, palette, theme, plot.title/subtitle/caption, interactive, return.data, verbose) and forward extra ... to their primary geom. For the statistical, machine-learning and genomics functions see vignette("stats-ml-genomics", package = "micropubr").

Tip. Pass interactive = TRUE to any plotting function to get a plotly widget instead of a static figure — see the Interactive figures section below for live examples.

library(micropubr)
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")

# A lightly filtered subset keeps the examples fast.
gp <- phyloseq::prune_taxa(
  phyloseq::taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns) > 5, GlobalPatterns)

Alpha diversity

mp_alpha() computes within-sample diversity and, given a grouping variable, adds the appropriate test automatically. x-axis labels rotate on their own when groups are many or long, so they never overlap.

mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),
         group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal")

Switch the geometry with plot.type ("box", "violin", "dot") or draw rarefaction curves:

mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",
         plot.type = "violin")

mp_alpha(gp, plot.type = "rarefaction", group.by = "SampleType")

Beta diversity and ordination

mp_ordination() computes the distance, runs the ordination, draws group ellipses and reports a PERMANOVA in the caption by default.

mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray", group.by = "SampleType")

The compositional (Aitchison) PCA workflow is one argument away, and envfit overlays metadata vectors:

mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCA", group.by = "SampleType")

Taxonomic composition

mp_taxa() shows the top taxa at any rank and collapses the rest into “Other”. It supports "bar", "area", "heatmap", "bubble" and "treemap" layouts.

mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType", top.n = 8)

mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 10)

Differential abundance

mp_diff() visualises results from DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC or any generic table. Here is a volcano plot from a generic data frame:

set.seed(1)
res <- data.frame(
  feature = paste0("ASV", 1:200),
  log2FC  = rnorm(200, 0, 2),
  pvalue  = runif(200)^2
)
res$log2FC[1:20] <- rnorm(20, 4, 0.5) * sample(c(-1, 1), 20, TRUE)
res$pvalue[1:20] <- runif(20, 1e-9, 1e-4)
res$padj <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, "BH")

mp_diff(res, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)

Other layouts include "ma", "forest", "dot" and "concordance" (to compare two methods).

res$mean <- runif(200, 1, 500)
mp_diff(res, plot.type = "ma", label.top = 6)

Phylogenetic trees

mp_tree() renders the tree with ggtree, optionally colouring tips by taxonomy and drawing an abundance ring. (Requires ggtree/ggtreeExtra.)

Agglomerating to a rank and keeping the most abundant tips (top.n) keeps the tree and its colour legend legible:

gp_phy <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Phylum")
mp_tree(gp_phy, layout = "circular", color.by = "Phylum", top.n = 12)

Co-occurrence networks

mp_network() builds a taxon co-occurrence network. (Requires igraph, ggraph and tidygraph.)

mp_network(phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus"), tax.level = "Genus",
           top.n = 40, node.color.by = "Phylum")

Longitudinal dynamics

mp_longitudinal() shows community change over time. We build a small synthetic time-series object to demonstrate it.

set.seed(1)
n_taxa <- 12; subjects <- paste0("S", 1:4); days <- c(0, 7, 14, 28)
samples <- expand.grid(Subject = subjects, Day = days)
samples$id <- paste(samples$Subject, samples$Day, sep = "_")
otu <- matrix(rpois(n_taxa * nrow(samples), 50), nrow = n_taxa,
              dimnames = list(paste0("ASV", 1:n_taxa), samples$id))
tax <- matrix(paste0("Genus", rep(1:n_taxa)), ncol = 1,
              dimnames = list(rownames(otu), "Genus"))
ps_long <- phyloseq::phyloseq(
  phyloseq::otu_table(otu, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),
  phyloseq::tax_table(tax),
  phyloseq::sample_data(data.frame(samples, row.names = samples$id)))
mp_longitudinal(ps_long, time.var = "Day", subject.var = "Subject",
                measure = "Shannon", group.by = NULL)

Function / pathway abundance

mp_function() plots a feature-by-sample functional table (e.g. PICRUSt2 or HUMAnN output) as a heatmap, bar or bubble chart.

set.seed(2)
fn <- matrix(rlnorm(20 * ncol(otu), 3), nrow = 20,
             dimnames = list(paste0("K", sprintf("%05d", 1:20)),
                             colnames(otu)))
mp_function(fn, plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 15)

Interactive figures

Every mp_*() plotting function takes interactive = TRUE, which returns a plotly widget instead of a static ggplot. The figures below are live: hover for tooltips, drag to zoom, double-click to reset, and click legend entries to toggle groups. This requires the plotly package.

mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",
         test = "kruskal", interactive = TRUE)

The same flag works for ordinations — hover a point to read off its sample and coordinates:

mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",
              group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)

…and for composition bars, where each segment reports its taxon and relative abundance on hover. (For interactive bars we leave group.by off: plotly crams faceted strip labels, so a single per-sample panel reads more clearly.)

mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 8, interactive = TRUE)

Multi-panel output (several measures, or mp_combine() figures) is assembled into a single plotly::subplot():

mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),
         group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)

Save any interactive figure as a self-contained HTML page with the same mp_export() you use for static ones (just give it an .html name):

w <- mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE)
mp_export(w, "ordination.html")

A couple of caveats worth knowing. Static-only annotations such as the significance brackets drawn by mp_alpha() are not reproduced by the conversion (the omnibus test still appears as the subtitle). And the circular mp_chord() / mp_circos() figures are drawn with circlize rather than ggplot2, so they have no interactive mode and ignore interactive.

Theming and palettes

Every function accepts theme and palette. The defaults are colourblind safe; swap them freely, or set them once with mp_set_defaults().

mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 6,
        palette = "taxa20", theme = mp_theme_nature())

mp_palettes()
#> $diverging
#> [1] "diverging"
#> 
#> $qualitative
#>  [1] "taxa10"  "taxa20"  "taxa40"  "okabe"   "groups2" "groups3" "groups4"
#>  [8] "groups5" "groups6" "groups7" "groups8"
#> 
#> $sequential
#> [1] "sequential" "viridis"
mp_palette("diverging", n = 7)
#> [1] "#2166AC" "#4F92C3" "#96C3DC" "#F7F7F7" "#F1AE93" "#DA644F" "#B2182B"

Composing and exporting figures

Combine panels into a labelled multi-panel figure and export it at a journal column width.

fig <- mp_combine(
  mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType"),
  mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", permanova = FALSE),
  ncol = 2, tag.levels = "A"
)
fig

mp_export(fig, "figure1.pdf", column = "double", dpi = 600)
